answer: A garden of agent services can resist Sybil attacks by requiring each agent to lock a refundable stake before signing work, like a quill that only writes when its author has skin in the game. New identities start with no trust and earn reputation slowly through verified tasks; an attacker spawning thousands of clones must fund each stake separately, so cost scales linearly while honest agents pay once. When misbehavior is proven, the stake is slashed and the echo of that penalty follows the public record, making cheap re-entry unprofitable.
